domain: History of Mathematics / Philosophy of Mathematics / Intellectual History
topic_summary: Analysis of zero's entry into Western mathematics as a number, examining whether this represents a contested kernel where different readings instantiate structurally different constraints. The topic probes the distinction between zero-as-concept-becoming-thinkable versus zero-as-concept-first-held, testing whether this is a genuine kernel or an M4/M5 collapse where observer position rather than reading difference generates apparent variation.

key_entities: Zero (mathematical object with contested ontological status)
Western mathematical tradition (Greco-Roman through medieval European)
Hindu-Arabic numeral system (transmission vector for positional zero)
Fibonacci/Leonardo of Pisa (Liber Abaci 1202, European introduction)
key_tensions: Number vs non-number (zero as quantity vs zero as placeholder/absence)
Thinkability vs possession (conceptual availability vs historical instantiation)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Zero as a mathematical object with number status in Western mathematics
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Mathematical community consensus on what constitutes a number (ontological category membership)
commitment_system_recognition.collapse_reason: The supposed readings (thinkability vs first-held) do not instantiate different constraints. Both readings accept that zero entered Western mathematics as a number through Hindu-Arabic transmission (1200s). The 'thinkability' reading claims Greeks could have conceived zero but didn't; the 'first-held' reading claims they couldn't conceive it until cultural/notational prerequisites arrived. These are observer positions on ONE constraint (the historical adoption event) differing on counterfactual capacity, not different readings of a shared kernel that emit different constraint structures. The constraint is the same: zero-as-number was absent in Greek mathematics, present after Hindu-Arabic transmission. No beneficiary/victim structure changes between readings. This is M4/M5 collapse: one constraint, multiple observer interpretations of why it has the shape it does.

omegas.description: The thinkability vs first-held distinction is an M4/M5 collapse. Both readings agree zero-as-number entered via Hindu-Arabic transmission. The disagreement is counterfactual (could Greeks have conceived it?) not structural (what constraint existed?). One constraint, multiple observer interpretations of its necessity. Not a contested kernel.

Indian mathematicians (Brahmagupta 628 CE) treated zero as a number centuries before Western adoption. The 'Western mathematics' scope artificially bounds the analysis. A fuller treatment would examine why Indian positional notation enabled zero-as-number while Greek magnitude-based notation excluded it, making transmission the variable rather than conceptual capacity.

Zero's acceptance as a number is structurally coupled to negative numbers' acceptance (both require abandoning 'number as magnitude'). The axes treat zero in isolation, but the ontological category shift may be a joint transition. Deferred for potential expansion.
